text: I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are presenting with hematuria and right flank pain; to determine the cause, I need to ask a few questions. First, how sudden was the onset of this pain, and would you describe it as a constant dull ache or a sharp, colicky pain that comes in waves?

speaker: Patient
text: 42-year-old Caucasian male. The patient reports experiencing visible blood in his urine accompanied by discomfort in his right flank. He denies any recent trauma to the area. He mentions a series of urinary tract infections over the past few years but has not been on renal dialysis.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Kidney Stone (Nephrolithiasis)

The presence of visible hematuria combined with right flank pain and a history of urinary tract infections is highly suggestive of a kidney stone. To confirm this and assess the stone's size and location, I will need to request imaging.

REQUEST IMAGES: Right_KUB_XRay AND Right_Abdomen_US
